name: Böe
prior: Selfridge/Moffat/Reiss/Avital, 'Real-time physical model of an Aeolian harp', ICSV24 2017: semi-empirical fluid model, Strouhal ~0.2, lock-in band at reduced velocity ~0.8-1.27 around each natural frequency, lock-in on higher harmonics, hysteresis from several shedding modes, sigmoids fitted to published plots; listening test: as good as a non-physical method, less authentic than recordings (VS: ioa.org.uk PDF, qmro.qmul.ac.uk, napier-repository.worktribe.com/output/3010509) = the direct ancestor, academic. Selfridge blog 2016 Pd patch: up to 13 strings, white noise through bandpasses per harmonic, brown-noise wake (VS: rodselfridge.wordpress.com/2016/11/23). Quilcom SIM-WINDHARP (free Windows VST, FlowStone): aeolian harp + wind + rustling, sidechain wind-speed input only (VS: plugins4free.com/plugin/3667). Soundiron Aeolian Fan Harp (Kontakt, sampled). Electrum Modular 'modular Aeolian harp' 2025: 8-band filterbank + comparator + sequential switch, wind as CV, no hysteresis (VS: matrixsynth.com/2025/05). EAR Modular Windstring: 10-band wind-metaphor filterbank (VS: perfectcircuit.com). iOS 'Aeolian Harp' (2021): particle toy with sampled kalimba/koto (VS: apps.appfollow.io). WPI 'Pitch Controlled Aeolian Harp' 2024: mechatronic real harp. Common technique noise -> sympathetic resonators (lmdsp Superchord, EAE Prismatic Wall, Rings/Halos/Resonate sympathetic strings, Vendaval) = the timbre is a routine patch. Myzel Obertoene (APP 4030-4113): buzz + two bandpasses on harm(f,y), 'Wandern' random walk, follows y at once = the same player-facing rule. Not found: a playable touch instrument with lock-in/hysteresis, hanging chords and dead zones on phones or in any mainstream app, plugin or module.
costNotes: 16 complex-rotation resonators in one worklet node measured 0.61 units incl. node (R: webaudio.md section 4) -> ~0.034 per resonator: 8 strings 0.28, 14 strings 0.48. Node 0.06 + 3 k-rate params 0.09. Wind band as a JS biquad ~0.25; cheaper to reuse the Reso class with short T60 (~0.04) -> L1 ~0.5. Noise table + 8 excitation MACs ~0.03; lock-in state machine, Gaussian weights, random walk per block negligible. Total L1 ~0.68 (idea 0.6 optimistic by ~15 %); L3 (14 resonators, second wind band, stereo) ~1.15-1.25 (idea 1.0). Phone factor x1.0-1.5. Native fallback possible (noise -> 8 gain -> 8 high-Q biquads + wind bandpass ~19 nodes ~0.6 units) but the capture/hysteresis state needs a main-thread timer per voice -> worklet is the right tool, native only as fallback. Numerics: T60 6 s -> r = 1 - 2.4e-5 per sample, doubles in locals, per-block denormal flush.
soundHeld: Conditionally distinctive. As specified it fails: the Gaussian e_k = exp(-((f_shed - k f)/(0.12 k f))^2) has 1 sigma = +-12 % of k*f, so from k ~ 4 upward neighbouring harmonics are excited together and the top register is a noisy cluster, not a singing string (the dead zones vanish). Fix: one-mode capture state machine (captured k gets full excitation, f_shed pulled onto k*f, neighbours leak <= -20 dB); chords then come from memory (T60 of previously captured strings) - the actually novel sound. Also 10-60 s random-walk orbits + +-20 % hysteresis mean nothing happens in a 2-10 s hold and a wide capture band makes the sound ignore the finger, then jump: y must drive f_shed directly, random walk small and 5-20 s, Fang default ~0.3. Fundamental always excited is physically wrong, musically right. Level depends on T60 (noise-driven RMS ~ sqrt(Q)): normalise excitation per mode so Nachklang is a timbre knob, not a volume knob.
soundBurst: Collapses to Hauch as specified: hit() gate 0.22 s (APP 5083), burstEnv closes v.out after the gate (APP 3517); a T60 4 s resonator reaches 32 % of steady state in 220 ms only if parked on one harmonic, a wind sweep across 8 harmonics gives each ~27 ms -> ~5 %, ringing ~25 dB under the held level, masked by the whoosh = Hauch's burst. Fix: 'gust pluck' burst mode - excitation x10-20 during the gate (vel-scaled), f_shed parked on harm(y) or stepping over 2-3 harmonics, noise impulse into all modes at onset, T60 capped ~1.5 s and rel <= 2 s like Obertoene (APP 4112); otherwise 8 hits/s x 5.5 s voice life = 44 live voices ~30 units, far over the 14-unit mobile budget (APP 2084).
failureModes: Gaussian width +-12 % of k*f smears harmonics >= 4 into a cluster; needs one-mode capture with leak
Puls hit cannot charge 4 s strings in a 0.22 s gate -> Hauch whoosh; needs gust-pluck burst mode with x10 excitation, capped T60, rel <= 2 s (else ~30 units of live voices)
Held note feels dead (10-60 s orbits) or ignores the finger then jumps (wide capture band); y must drive f_shed directly, orbit 5-20 s, Fang ~0.3
Timbre sameness with Obertoene/Hauch unless strings ring after the wind leaves and the capture jump is a clear event
Level varies > 10 dB with T60 and k; normalise excitation per mode (~sqrt(alpha_k), 1/sqrt(k))
Fundamental always excited is a physical liberty to be labelled
Wind band on top of the resonators doubles the price unless it reuses the Reso class
verdict: Rare, not new: the lock-in aeolian harp is a published, downloadable Pd model (Selfridge et al. 2016/17) and exists as one obscure Windows VST, but no playable touch instrument has it, and the capture/memory behaviour is a real gap in the catalogue. Worklet-feasible at about 0.7 units (0.5 if the wind band reuses the resonator class), L3 about 1.2. As specified it will fail twice: the +-12 %*k Gaussian smears the upper register into a cluster (replace with one-mode capture + leak), and the 0.22 s Puls hit cannot charge 4 s strings so it degenerates into a Hauch whoosh (needs a gust-pluck burst mode with x10 excitation and a capped T60). With those two fixes and y-driven wind, it is a distinct engine; without them it is Obertoene with noise.
